title: Behavioral Interviews & Staff-Level Competencies
summary: The round where strong coders get rejected and Staff offers get won. It is a structured test of how you create impact through other people — not small talk.

blocks.markdown:
The behavioral round predicts how you'll behave on the job by mining your past.

- Built on one finding: **past behavior predicts future behavior** far better than hypotheticals.
- Screens fixed **dimensions**: impact, scope, ownership, leadership, collaboration, conflict, ambiguity.
- At senior+ levels it is often the **deciding** round — prepare it like system design.
- Strong answers carry **numbers, conflict, and a decision you owned**. Weak ones are vague and all-positive.

blocks.subTitle: Which story to reach for
blocks.markdown:
Match the story to the question's dimension — don't default to your favorite.

| Question | Reach for |
|---|---|
| "A time you led…" | Drove without authority |
| "A conflict…" | Resolved with data, not winning |
| "Biggest failure?" | Real failure + what you changed |
| Targeting Staff | Org-wide, cross-team impact |

blocks.subTitle: It's a rubric, not a chat
blocks.markdown:
The interviewer arrives with a leveling rubric and a list of dimensions to probe.

- They ask an open question targeting one dimension, then silently map your words onto the rubric.
- **Follow-ups are where scoring happens**: "why that choice?", "what did they say?", "what would you do differently?".
- Rehearsed stories collapse under probing — real ones get richer.
- Goal of the structure: two interviewers scoring the same story should land close.

blocks.subTitle: The dimensions probed
blocks.markdown:
Each question targets one or two of these signals.

- **Impact** — did it matter, in numbers, money, users, time saved?
- **Scope** — your task, your team, or the whole org?
- **Ownership** — did you own the outcome end to end, including the not-your-job parts?
- **Leadership** — did you drive people and decisions, often without authority?
- **Collaboration** — do others want to work with you?
- **Conflict** — did you resolve disagreement constructively, not by winning?
- **Ambiguity** — can you define a fuzzy problem before solving it?

blocks.subTitle: STAR makes you legible
blocks.markdown:
STAR is the format that lets the rubric score your story.

![STAR answer structure](assets/d11-behavioral-staff-competencies/star-structure.svg)

- **Situation** and **Task** — quick context, set the scene.
- **Action** — the bulk of your airtime, what *you* personally did.
- **Result** — crisp, with real before-and-after numbers.
- A good answer runs **2–4 minutes** — deep enough to show substance, short enough to leave room for follow-ups.

blocks.subTitle: The scope ladder
blocks.markdown:
Scope is the main axis that separates levels.

![Scope ladder from mid to staff](assets/d11-behavioral-staff-competencies/scope-ladder.svg)

- **Mid** — I deliver my own tasks well (individual).
- **Senior** — I make my team succeed and mentor others (team).
- **Staff** — I multiply many engineers and set direction (org).
- A beautifully-executed **solo feature is a Senior-and-below story**, however well told.
- A real Staff story has you operating **without formal authority**.

blocks.subTitle: "I" vs "we", confidence vs humility
blocks.markdown:
Telling a story means balancing real tensions.

| Tension | Resolve by |
|---|---|
| "I" vs "we" | "We" for context, "I" for actions |
| Confidence vs humility | Own decisions, credit others |
| Polished vs authentic | Prep structure + numbers, not a script |

Breadth shows scope but sounds shallow; depth shows competence but sounds small — pick a story with both.

blocks.subTitle: Picking the right story
blocks.markdown:
Plain rules for choosing what to tell.

- If the question **names a dimension**, tell a story whose Action proves exactly that — not your favorite.
- Targeting **Staff** → prefer cross-team or org impact over a deeper single-team story.
- Asked for a **failure** → a real one with real cost, then the concrete change. "I work too hard" is an instant red flag.
- Got **one strong number**? Lead the Result with it. One real metric beats three vague claims.

blocks.subTitle: How the big loops score it
blocks.markdown:
Every company turns the same machinery into its own rubric.

- **Amazon** — 16 Leadership Principles as the explicit rubric; a **Bar Raiser** with veto guards consistency. Name the principle and feed clean STAR evidence.
- **Google** — scores go to a **hiring committee** that reads packets, so written-friendly STAR clarity matters even more.
- **Meta** — "Driving Results"; the level decision hinges on scope evidence in your stories.
- **Netflix** — high talent density means the behavioral bar *is* the hiring bar.

blocks.subTitle: The must-prep questions
blocks.markdown:
A handful of questions appear in almost every loop — polish them cold.

- **"Most significant project and your role?"** — most-asked; pick a story matching your target scope.
- **"A disagreement you resolved?"** — seek to understand, bring data, stay intact. "Disagree and commit" is a great closer.
- **"Your biggest failure?"** — real cost, no blame, spend the back half on what you changed.
- **"Led without authority?"** — the core Staff signal: align people who don't report to you.
- Build a **story bank** of 8–12 real stories, each tagged to the dimensions it proves.

blocks.subTitle: Signals it's working
blocks.markdown:
Read the room — and read your actual operating.

- **Follow-ups go deeper, not wider** → your story is rich and credible. Bailing to a new topic means it fell flat.
- You answer **"what would you do differently?" instantly** → the tell of real reflection.
- On the job, **your work outlives you**: a standard set, a library teams adopt unprompted.
- **Engineers level up around you** and other teams pull you into their decisions — your scope crossed the team boundary.

The beliefs that sink strong engineers:

- **"It's just a vibe check."** At senior+ it's often the deciding round.
- **"Saying 'we' shows I'm a team player."** Overusing "we" erases you — the interviewer scores one person.
- **"My best story is my most technical one."** No — the best story matches the dimension *asked* and the level *targeted*.
- **"Only tell clean, positive stories."** Stories with no tension are unbelievable.
- **"Staff is Senior with harder coding."** It's scope and multiplication, not raw depth.
- **"Failure questions are traps."** A well-told real failure is one of your strongest signals.
